incidents.description: Google leaked routes learned from peers and customers to Verizon, which propagated them. Japanese networks were worst affected, NTT OCN most of all.
Amazon Route 53 DNS prefixes were announced by eNET, redirecting MyEtherWallet users to an attacker-controlled DNS server.

A BGP optimizer at DQE Communications generated more-specific routes, which were announced to its customer Allegheny Technologies and then to its other transit provider Verizon, which propagated them worldwide.
Vodafone Idea began originating tens of thousands of routes that do not belong to it, which propagated through its upstream Bharti Airtel.

An attacker used credentials found online to log into Orange España's RIPE NCC account and publish ROAs naming the wrong origin AS, which made much of the operator's own address space RPKI-invalid and therefore unroutable for networks that filter.

incidents.note: no elevation in routes relayed through the culprit during the incident
incidents.description: Cox Communications announced several thousand additional routes in two bursts an hour apart.

incidents.note: no elevation in routes relayed through the culprit during the incident
incidents.description: A routing policy change at a Cloudflare router in Miami became too permissive and redistributed internally learned prefixes to all BGP neighbours at that location, including transit providers and peers.

notes: Only route leaks can be judged this way. An origin hijack travels an ordinary-looking path and in an RPKI misuse incident the routing was correct, so neither is something a path-based detector could find; both are reported as not applicable, never as misses.
'not visible' means the collectors used never saw the leak, which is a statement about where the vantage points are and not about the detector.
Recall here rests on a denominator of two. It is a count, not an estimate.
